sets.relationshipLabel: a stage tool, then the action it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A microphone exists to amplify a voice, just as a fog machine exists to obscure the stage, tool named before its purpose.

sets.relationshipLabel: a stage category, and a kind of thing within it
sets.explanation: A skull is a kind of prop and an ingenue is a kind of role, category named first and the specific instance second.

sets.relationshipLabel: the same kind of theatrical thing, smaller then larger
sets.explanation: A black box theater scales up to a Broadway house just as a one-act scales up to a full-length, each pair moving from small to large on its own axis.

sets.relationshipLabel: two theatre spaces defined by touching, where one ends and the other begins
sets.explanation: The green room opens directly onto backstage just as the catwalk sits flush against the grid, each pair a boundary between adjoining spaces.

glossary.definition: The framework of beams high above a stage ceiling, used to hang lights and scenery from up top.

definitions.definition: A handheld or clipped-on device that picks up your voice so the whole room can hear it.
To make a sound bigger and louder so it carries further.
A machine that puffs out mist to give the stage atmosphere or hide something from view.
To hide or blur something so it's hard to see clearly.
Any object an actor carries or uses on stage, from a teacup to a sword.
A stage object shaped like a human head bone, often used for dramatic effect.
A character an actor plays in a show.
A young, innocent female character type often cast in plays.
A small, bare, flexible performance space with movable seating and no fixed stage.
A big, grand commercial theater built for large professional productions.
A short play performed in a single continuous piece without intermission.
A full evening's play, usually broken into acts with an intermission.
The lounge where performers relax and wait before or after going on stage.
The area behind and around the stage where performers and crew work out of audience view.
A narrow walkway high above the stage used to reach lights and rigging.
The framework of beams high above a stage ceiling, used to hang lights and scenery from up top.
